reference.title: Complete vs incomplete intestinal metaplasia
reference.intro: Subtype on H&E; use AB-PAS (± HID) when uncertain. Report the highest-risk subtype present when mixed.

groups.heading: Complete (type I)
points: Small-bowel phenotype: goblet cells alternating with eosinophilic absorptive cells
Well-defined brush border (PAS-positive magenta line on AB-PAS)
Paneth cells often present at crypt bases
Goblet mucin is sialomucin (blue on AB-PAS); no mucin in the intervening columnar cells

images.caption: H&E: goblet cells between absorptive cells with a crisp luminal brush border; Paneth cells at crypt bases.
images.credit: Aumpan et al., PLoS ONE 2020, Fig 4A (cropped)

images.caption: AB-PAS: blue goblet cells (white arrow) with a magenta brush border (black arrow) on the absorptive cells.
images.credit: Tjandra et al., Cancers 2023, Fig 3 left (cropped)

images.caption: AB-PAS, type I: magenta brush border between blue/purple goblet cells.

groups.heading: Incomplete (type II/III)
points: Colonic phenotype: goblet cells of varying size among mucin-secreting columnar cells
No brush border; irregular, pale mucin droplets in the columnar cells
Paneth cells absent or sparse
Type II: columnar cells contain neutral mucin or sialomucin (magenta / blue on AB-PAS); type III: sulphomucin (brown-black on HID) — higher cancer risk

images.caption: H&E: goblet cells among columnar cells with apical mucin vacuoles of variable size; no brush border.
images.credit: Aumpan et al., PLoS ONE 2020, Fig 4C (cropped)

images.caption: AB-PAS: acidic (blue) mucin in the columnar cells (yellow arrow); no brush border.
images.credit: Tjandra et al., Cancers 2023, Fig 3 right (cropped)

images.caption: AB-PAS, type II: mucus-producing columnar cells (neutral magenta or blue sialomucin) between goblet cells.
HID-AB, type III: brown-black sulphomucin in the columnar cells.

fields.label: Mucin histochemistry
fields.help: Adds a histochemistry line to the microscopy when performed.

fields.label: Polyp / adenoma
fields.help: Leads the diagnosis line; grade any dysplasia in the field below.

reference.title: Gastric polyps and adenomas
reference.intro: Key features from Pathology Outlines, StatPearls and Gastric Adenomas and Mimickers (Diagnostics, 2026). Dysplasia, when present, is graded low or high. WHO 6th edition (2026) folds intestinal-type and foveolar-type adenomas into gastric dysplasia (MAPS III); pyloric and oxyntic gland adenomas stay separate.

groups.heading: Hyperplastic polyp
points: Elongated, tortuous, cystically dilated foveolar pits with apical mucin
Oedematous, inflamed lamina propria with strands of smooth muscle
Regenerative atypia matures toward the surface; dysplasia involves the surface and begins abruptly

groups.heading: Fundic gland polyp
points: Cystically dilated oxyntic glands lined by parietal, chief and mucous foveolar cells
Parietal-cell hyperplasia with apocrine snouting on proton-pump inhibitors
Dysplasia is rare in sporadic polyps and commoner in FAP

groups.heading: Intestinal-type adenoma
points: Dysplastic columnar epithelium with goblet and Paneth cells; no apical mucin cap
MUC2 and CDX2 positive, with apical CD10
Background chronic gastritis with intestinal metaplasia may be present

groups.heading: Foveolar-type adenoma
points: Dysplastic foveolar epithelium with an apical mucin cap
Diffuse MUC5AC
Background mucosa usually without inflammation, atrophy or metaplasia; hybrid intestinal and gastric phenotypes occur

groups.heading: Pyloric gland adenoma
points: Closely packed pyloric-type glands with eosinophilic, ground-glass cytoplasm and no apical mucin cap
Diffuse MUC6; MUC5AC mostly confined to the surface
Seen without dysplasia or with low or high grade dysplasia, and can be associated with adenocarcinoma

groups.heading: Oxyntic gland adenoma
points: Deep-mucosal, branching and anastomosing glands of chief cells with basophilic cytoplasm
No more than mild atypia; the surface foveolae may be spared
Pepsinogen I and MUC6 positive; diffuse strong cyclin D1 helps separate it from normal oxyntic glands in biopsies
Submucosal invasion makes it an adenocarcinoma of fundic-gland type

groups.heading: Inflammatory fibroid polyp
points: Submucosal spindle and stellate cells with onion-skin cuffing of thin-walled vessels
Oedematous stroma rich in eosinophils; minimal mitotic activity
CD34 positive, KIT negative

fields.label: Carcinoma type (WHO)
options: Poorly cohesive carcinoma, signet-ring cell type
Poorly cohesive carcinoma, non-signet-ring cell type
fields.help: WHO Digestive System Tumours, 6th edition (2026). Prints in place of the dysplasia / malignancy value, with a short morphology sentence.

fields.label: Differentiation
fields.help: Tubular and papillary types, and adenocarcinoma whose subtype is not assessable. CAP grades by gland formation: well (more than 95% glands), moderately (50 to 95%) or poorly differentiated (49% or less).

is: Poorly cohesive carcinoma, signet-ring cell type
Poorly cohesive carcinoma, non-signet-ring cell type

fields.label: HER2 IHC (4B5)
fields.help: Biopsy scoring: a cluster of at least 5 tumour cells, whatever the percentage stained (CAP).

reference.title: HER2 in gastric biopsies
reference.intro: CAP gastric HER2 template (ToGA criteria). Biopsy: a cancer-cell cluster of at least 5 cells, whatever the percentage stained; resection: 10% of cancer cells. Membranous staining only.

groups.heading: Score 0 (negative)
points: No reactivity, or no membranous reactivity in any cancer cell

groups.heading: Score 1+ (negative)
points: A cluster with faint or barely perceptible membranous reactivity

groups.heading: Score 2+ (equivocal)
points: A cluster with weak to moderate complete, basolateral or lateral membranous reactivity
Reflex to ISH

groups.heading: Score 3+ (positive)
points: A cluster with strong complete, basolateral or lateral membranous reactivity

groups.heading: Dual ISH
points: Amplified at a HER2/CEP17 ratio of 2.0 or more
Record the average HER2 signals per cell and the ratio

optionLabels.Background lymphoid cells only: Positive in background lymphoid cells only

reference.title: EBER in situ hybridisation
reference.intro: EBV-associated gastric carcinoma is defined by EBER in the tumour cells.

groups.heading: Positive
points: Nuclear signal in the tumour cells
Common in carcinoma with lymphoid stroma: syncytial growth, poorly formed glands and a dense lymphoid stroma without desmoplasia

groups.heading: Negative
points: No signal in the tumour cells; positive background lymphoid cells alone do not make the carcinoma EBV-associated

fields.label: PD-L1 IHC
fields.help: Prints the CPS with its clone and no positive or negative label: the cut-off depends on the drug.

reference.title: PD-L1 combined positive score
reference.intro: CPS: PD-L1-staining tumour cells, lymphocytes and macrophages, divided by the viable tumour cells, times 100 (22C3 gastric manual), recorded from 0 to 100. The report prints the CPS and clone without a positive or negative label, because the cut-off depends on the drug.

groups.heading: Cut-offs in use
points: US labels for pembrolizumab and nivolumab in HER2-negative disease: CPS 1 or more (2025)
22C3 gastric manual: PD-L1 expression at CPS 1 or more
A 2026 biomarker review: pembrolizumab CPS 10 or more, nivolumab CPS 5 or more, tislelizumab tumour area positivity 5% or more
The QMH stomach biomarker page groups at CPS 10

groups.heading: Clones
points: The QMH page lists 22C3 (Dako) and E1L3N (Cell Signaling)
28-8 and SP263 are offered for results from other laboratories

reference.title: Claudin 18.2 (VENTANA CLDN18, 43-14A)
reference.intro: Roche interpretation guide; the FDA-approved test for zolbetuximab. QMH records the moderate (2+) and strong (3+) percentages.

groups.heading: Positive
points: 75% or more of viable tumour cells with moderate to strong (2+ or 3+) membranous staining

groups.heading: Negative
points: Fewer than 75% of viable tumour cells with moderate to strong membranous staining

groups.heading: Scoring
points: At least 50 viable tumour cells
Membranous staining only; cytoplasmic staining is not scored
Normal gastric mucosa is the internal positive control

presets.help: A1 antrum GC, A2 antrum LC, A3 incisura, B1 body GC, B2 body LC — enables OLGA / OLGIM staging

presets.help: Three pooled containers as the LIS usually labels them

snippets.label: H. pylori — eradication
snippets.text: Helicobacter pylori organisms are identified. Eradication therapy and confirmation of clearance are suggested if not already undertaken.

snippets.label: H. pylori with intestinal metaplasia
snippets.text: Helicobacter pylori is present together with intestinal metaplasia. Eradication therapy with subsequent re-assessment of the metaplastic mucosa is suggested.

snippets.label: Incomplete IM — risk comment
snippets.text: Incomplete-type intestinal metaplasia is a recognised risk factor for gastric adenocarcinoma. Assessment of its extent on mapping biopsies (Sydney protocol) is suggested if not already performed.

snippets.label: High-stage OLGA / OLGIM — surveillance
snippets.text: Extensive / high-stage atrophic gastritis and intestinal metaplasia are associated with an increased risk of gastric adenocarcinoma; endoscopic surveillance at three-yearly intervals (MAPS II / BSG 2019) is suggested in the appropriate clinical context.

snippets.label: Incomplete mapping — repeat Sydney biopsies
snippets.text: Intestinal metaplasia is present but the biopsies do not allow OLGA / OLGIM staging. Mapping biopsies according to the updated Sydney protocol (antrum x2, incisura, body x2) are suggested if surveillance is being considered.
